results.rationale: To set up a tangent equation you need the line through the touching point with slope f'(x0): a line equation from a slope and one point. In the catalog only ae772695 (J8) develops this, and nothing on the current path secures equations of linear functions. The edge points backwards (J8 → E), both goals apply in all 16 states, and it matches the Hessen KC E.2 bullet 'Gleichung von Tangente und Normale' (p. 32).
results.concerns: 0264591c is close to a union of f042385e (tangent equations) and 6aed5be9 (slope angles). The parallel edges (1/13, 2/6) come from this duplication; merging the E tangent block would be cleaner.

results.rationale: The slope angle is α = arctan m, an angle taken from a tangent ratio in the slope triangle. In the catalog only 71a483ba (J9) develops this. The E goal 6aed5be9 also computes slope angles, but it lacks the same trigonometry basis (candidate 6). The edge points backwards and the jurisdictions are identical.
results.concerns: This edge parallels candidate 6. If the tangent block were merged, one edge to 71a483ba would cover both.

results.rationale: Each Newton step takes the zero of the tangent at the current graph point, so the tangent equation is needed. f042385e develops it in E; the Hessen KC places it in E.2 (p. 32) and Newton in E.6 (p. 34). 0264591c would also work but adds slope angles, and the forced drop of the direct edge to b1dcc191 changes nothing that is secured.
results.concerns: The zero of the tangent also needs the zero of a linear function. 4acca6ef (Nullstellen linearer Funktionen berechnen, J8) stays unsecured even with candidates 3 and 13.

results.rationale: Solving a simple extreme-value problem means setting up a target function from the situation and solving f'(x) = 0, a linear or quadratic equation. Today the secured set holds no algebra beyond grade 6. a7ccb7a9 is the Sek I forerunner (modelling with quadratic functions including extreme values) and secures term translation and linear and quadratic equations transitively. 1b70498a (E.1 modelling) is on the E path but is about choosing a model and fitting parameters, not optimisation.
results.concerns: The extremum criterion (sign change of f', 350fc8b1) is secured only qualitatively, via 845440ce. That gap is outside this candidate.

results.rationale: An angle between two graphs is the difference of two slope angles, so the step from slope to angle is needed. 6aed5be9 is the E goal that develops exactly this step, earlier on the same path. Its own arctan basis depends on candidate 6.
results.concerns: This only works together with candidate 6; without it, 56b4acb5 would need a direct edge to 71a483ba. 6aed5be9 overlaps 7c0dee9b, which is already required. The intersection point itself (0b23413e) is not secured for 56b4acb5 either. The forced removal at 1675fdde is harmless.

results.rationale: Computing 'zugehörige Steigungswinkel' needs tan α = m and the inverse tangent. In the catalog only 71a483ba (J9) develops this. The edge points backwards (J9 → E) and the jurisdictions are identical.
results.concerns: 6aed5be9 is close to 7c0dee9b plus slope angles (duplication in the tangent block).

results.rationale: The goal chooses and applies derivative rules. The power, factor and sum rules are developed in dde9ae98 (which requires e9445479, the power rule), matching Hessen KC E.2 (p. 32). The broader 623cd47f also requires dde9ae98, so dde9ae98 is the narrowest sufficient goal, and there is no cycle.
results.concerns: 858113c5 is a hub: 236 goals gain two E.2 goals. Its polynomial part largely duplicates 623cd47f.

results.rationale: Derivatives of exponential functions are developed by c3c057a3, which requires this goal through 3a5bf7e5 → 8fa32a68 → 858113c5, so reordering is impossible. The Hessen KC also places the derivative of e^x in E.4 (p. 33), after the E.2 rules for x^n with integer n, the factor and sum rules, and polynomials (p. 32). Drop 'Exponential- und' so the description reads '... bis Grad 3 sowie einfachen Potenzfunktionen ...'; c3c057a3 still covers the exponential part.
results.concerns: The changed description needs a new review. After narrowing, it is worth checking whether 8fa32a68 (properties of a^x) still needs its edge to 858113c5.

results.rationale: Reconstructing a polynomial function means setting up and solving a linear system with three or four unknowns. Nothing secured goes beyond single linear equations, and 546bf0b3 (J8) covers only simple two-variable systems. 5743b8f9 develops exactly linear systems with three unknowns for function coefficients; the only other such goals are in Q2, which would point forwards.
results.concerns: The edge extends the scope to DE-SH. The SH Fachanforderungen Mathematik 2024 put hand-solving of linear systems with an algorithmic method (the Gauß idea) in Sek II (p. 61) and only two-variable systems in Sek I (p. 38). In SH a J9-labelled goal would become a prerequisite: the content is needed there, but the grade label does not fit.

results.rationale: To justify the step from secant to tangent, the learner must read the difference quotient as the slope Δy/Δx of a straight line. The secured goal ae20183e covers the quotient but not that reading. 2d75fd3f (E review of slope and intercept) comes before E.2 on the E path, already requires the Sek I goal af3d6bff, and is sufficient.
results.concerns: af3d6bff (Lineare Funktionen beschreiben) would be an earlier and slightly narrower alternative; either is acceptable. 263 descendant goals gain 4 secured goals.

results.rationale: The description explicitly demands reflective use of digital tools to check results. 1eb7b2ce develops exactly that: plotting graphs, finding zeros and extrema numerically, and checking the results critically. 89ca5089 (plotting only) would be only partly sufficient, and 1eb7b2ce is an early E goal, so the edge points backwards.

The exemplary h-method proof for x^2 and x^3 requires expanding (x+h)^n and simplifying the difference quotient. e322310f develops the binomial formulas and term transformations and is the usual route. 959cc50b (distributive law) would also allow multiplying out, but it is not clearly better.
results.concerns: 'Ganzzahlige Exponenten' includes n < 0, which needs negative powers and fraction terms; 6596405a (Potenzgesetze mit ganzzahligen Exponenten anwenden, J8) stays unsecured. The forced removal at 'Erhaltung der mechanischen Energie tiefer verstehen (LK)' is harmless.

results.rationale: As in candidate 1, tangent and normal equations need a line equation from a slope and a point, which only ae772695 (J8) develops. This matches Hessen KC E.2 (p. 32). The edge points backwards and the jurisdictions are identical.
results.concerns: Normal equations also need the normal slope −1/m. It is developed in 7c0dee9b and 6aed5be9 but is not secured for f042385e.

results.otherGoalTitle: Ableitungsbegriff aus mittleren und momentanen Änderungsraten entwickeln
results.rationale: Reading instantaneous velocity as a tangent slope needs the concept that the rate at a point is the limit of secant slopes. 7156558c (J10, all 16 states) develops exactly this and comes earlier. 2143e9e8 is math E.2 material (Hessen math KC p. 32) and also pulls in the h-method goal b42bdfcc, while physics treats average versus instantaneous velocity in E.1 (Hessen physics KC p. 30). Physics E goals already link to math J10 goals (Bogenmaß, Logarithmus).
results.concerns: 322 physics goals gain 24 Sek I goals, and 10 direct edges become redundant and would be removed mechanically (e.g. 'Modellierung und Idealisierung von Bewegungen' → 'Terme mit Variablen lesen und deuten'). If the J10 calculus strand is not really taught in every state, 2143e9e8 is the fallback, but then math E.2 must come before physics E.1. Side effect: quadratic functions become secured for the uniform-acceleration chain.

results.rationale: Acceleration as a quantity is introduced only in e4b38061, which requires this goal (via 971beafa and bf8517a9), and no Sek I physics goal covers acceleration, so reordering is impossible. Drop 'und t-a-' so the goal reads '... in t-s- und t-v-Diagrammen darstellen und interpretieren'. Nothing is lost: e4b38061 already describes t-a representations, and the Hessen physics KC lists t-a diagrams and the definition of acceleration in the same Themenfeld E.1 (p. 30).
results.concerns: Reading t-v diagrams of non-uniform motion also relies on instantaneous velocity (bf8517a9, later). For 'einfache Bewegungen' this is acceptable because mean rate of change is secured, but the new description review should check it.

remarks: Most candidates have one cause: the E-phase analysis goals and the physics E kinematics goals barely build on lower secondary; their secured sets stop at grade 5-6 arithmetic plus 'Zuordnungen analysieren'.

More gaps of the same kind outside the pilot: zero of a line for Newton (4acca6ef), normal slope for f042385e, intersection point for 56b4acb5 (0b23413e), negative powers for e9445479 (6596405a). A systematic review of the E-phase entry points would be cheaper than single edges.
Near-duplicate atomic goals: 0264591c ≈ f042385e + 6aed5be9, 6aed5be9 ≈ 7c0dee9b + angles, 858113c5 vs 623cd47f; hence the parallel edges 1/13 and 2/6.
Dependencies: 5 needs 6 for the arctan basis; 3 needs 13 so that the tangent equation rests on the line equation.
The J10 and E calculus strands run in parallel, are unconnected and both marked for all 16 states; J10 applicability not checked against each state's source.
Sources read: Hessen math KC pp. 32-34, Hessen physics KC p. 30, SH Fachanforderungen Mathematik 2024 pp. 38 and 61 (all under curricula/DE/Gymnasium/input/).
Read requires edges with an own read-only script; did not run deriveKnowledgeContext.ts; changed no repository file.
